change: Store a full key tag and dense entry index in each ordered-map hash slot. Signed/unsigned 64-bit integer tags are exact keys and skip the dependent key-array read; other keys retain hash and equality.
decision: Keep: unchanged graph source improves materially on native and web; text and compiler CPU measurements do not show a broad regression. Accept the recorded memory cost.
full: Independent C bootstrap; 5483 passed in 167.28s, two pytest workers.
implementation_notes: The first keys/vals fields and insertion order are unchanged. Empty/tombstone state is separate from the tag, allowing every key/hash bit pattern.
Generic tags retain full 64-bit hashes; equal hashes still compare keys. Custom hash/equality callback cases pass.
Only comments changed after the measured compiler was built. New tests cover word boundaries, full-hash collisions, growth, compaction, reservation and independent copies.
memory_tradeoff: Slots grow from 8 to 16 bytes. Three alternating whole-process samples: graph peak RSS 223388 to 256156 KiB (+32 MiB, 14.7%); compiler 244388 to 244656 KiB.
timing_limits: Native and Node/WebAssembly, one Linux development host, CPU 2, alternating fresh processes. Graph size 1,000,000; text 10,000,000 tokens.
Three measured samples after one discarded process per variant. C graph uses a different flat representation and is not a language-only overhead comparison.

Compiler build comparison uses the same candidate source tree for both compilers. Five pairs; CPU medians +1.2% self-build, +1.3% tour, -0.8% Netpong. Wall times are noisy (load average around 6); self-build wall median rose 2.068 to 2.395 seconds while CPU rose 1.813 to 1.835 seconds.
Web runtime is Node/V8, not browser rendering. No cross-platform guarantee.
